results.title: How Stratified Random Sampling Works, With Examples
results.content: * A population is divided into groups that share characteristics called strata for stratified random sampling. Stratified random sampling involves dividing the entire population into homogeneous groups called strata, the plural of stratum. A stratified random sample divides the population into smaller groups or strata based on shared characteristics. Stratified random sampling ensures that each subgroup of a given population is adequately represented within the whole sample population of a research study. > **Proportionate stratified random sample = (Sample size / Population size) × Stratum size**. Stratified random sampling can't be used if researchers can’t confidently classify every member of the population into a subgroup. The research team has a proportionate stratified random sample of college students with these groups. Stratified random sampling is often used when researchers want to know about different subgroups or strata based on the entire population being studied.
